feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. The Integrator's evidence is iteration 6 (50 mm span, 12 mm footprint, y 0.05, base 1.15, kp 4.5, kd 0.45), which scored 355.3 with oval progress 0.956 and 17 of 20 oval finishes. Its s-bend and slalom max_error were 0.0682 and 0.0645 m, and neither track finished. Line losses stayed near 1 per run and steering oscillation stayed about 0.2 to 0.25, so the excursions are turn-induced rather than sensing dropouts. Iterations 0 to 6 show max_error on a 0.059 to 0.068 m plateau across every span, footprint, lead and controller change. This candidate therefore changes only wheel_track, from 0.12 to 0.10 m, and the Integrator scales kp to 3.75 to keep the steering gain near its proven level. Decide from the next race as follows. If s-bend and slalom max_error both fall below 0.06 m with oval progress at 0.65 or more, keep wheel_track 0.10 and tune the controller only. If oval progress falls below about 0.65 while steering oscillation rises above about 0.3, the steering gain is still too high, so keep wheel_track 0.10 and ask the Integrator to lower kp further. If max_error stays at or above 0.06 m on the s-bend and slalom while oval progress holds, the turn-rate change did not help, so the next geometry test is a sensor span change on the s-bend and slalom tracks.
requested_changes: If s-bend and slalom max_error are still at or above 0.06 m while oval progress holds at 0.65 or more, change the sensor span from 50 mm to 60 mm (x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03) with 12 mm footprints at y 0.05, keeping wheel_track 0.10. Iterations 2 and 3 showed 60 mm lowered line losses, so this tests whether a wider array reduces the bend excursions at the narrower track.

If oval progress falls below about 0.65 at wheel_track 0.10 with steering oscillation above about 0.3, keep wheel_track 0.10 and reduce the sensor lead from y 0.05 to y 0.04, which keeps the span. Iteration 1 showed that y 0.03 collapses progress, so do not go below 0.04.

Keep the 50 mm span, 12 mm footprint and y 0.05 unless one of the rules above applies. Iteration 4 (50 mm) and iteration 0 (40 mm) both reached oval progress above 0.66, and iteration 3 (60 mm, 12 mm) fell to 0.275, so do not move the span toward 60 mm without the evidence above.
